info.title: Nodes
info.description: Nodes is the registry of builds (jobs another tool runs on a machine, for example a compile on a build node) and of per-node build controls. A node is a machine Navigatorr knows (a transcode worker). For a node, the worker itself decides whether a build may run (its lease); this API only keeps the record, shows it, and lets an operator pause new builds on a node or cancel a build. Use GET /nodes/v1/nodes to pick a machine, POST /nodes/v1/builds to record a build on a machine that is not a node, GET /nodes/v1/builds to see what is running, POST /nodes/v1/builds/{id}/cancel to stop one. Errors are JSON {error, code, hint}; the hint names the endpoint to use instead.

get.summary: List nodes with their build and transcode state
get.description: Every machine Navigatorr knows as a node, sorted by name. For each: whether new builds are paused (builds_paused and since), the builds running on it, and, read from the transcode side, whether transcoding is paused or held. Call this first to choose a machine, or to see why a build was refused (builds_paused). Read-only.

parameters.name: transcode
parameters.description: Send false to leave out the transcode block: the transcode side is not asked at all.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

get.description: One node: builds pause (builds_paused, builds_paused_since), running builds and transcode state. 404 unknown_node if the name is not a configured node (list them with GET /nodes/v1/nodes). Read-only.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Node name, as listed by GET /nodes/v1/nodes.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

post.summary: Pause or resume new builds on a node
post.description: Sets whether the node accepts new builds. {"paused": true} makes the node's worker refuse new build leases (builds already running are not touched, and transcoding is not paused: use the transcode pause for that). {"paused": false} resumes. Idempotent: repeating a request changes nothing and keeps the pause start time. Returns the node as GET /nodes/v1/nodes/{name} would. Changes operator state: use only when asked.

paused.description: true to refuse new builds on the node, false to accept them again.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

get.description: Build records, newest created first, whatever their status: running and ended ones are in one order that never changes while you page, so a build that finishes between two pages is neither repeated nor skipped. Filter by node (the build's target machine), status (running, succeeded, failed, cancelled, lost; waiting only on old rows) and source (the tool that registered it). Paged: limit is 1 to 500 (default 50); pass next_cursor of one answer as cursor to get the next page; the last page has no next_cursor. A cursor stays valid even if the build it came from was pruned meanwhile. Use this to see what is running on a machine or to find the id to cancel. Read-only.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: Only builds whose target is this machine name.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only this status (waiting appears only on rows an earlier server left; Navigatorr cancels them).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Only builds registered by this tool.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 500 (default 50); outside that range is 400 invalid_request.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: next_cursor from the previous page (an opaque position: any well-formed value is accepted, and one that did not come from next_cursor simply starts from that position; only a malformed value is 400 invalid_cursor).

next_cursor.description: Present when more builds follow; pass it as cursor. Absent on the last page.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

post.summary: Register a build on a machine that is not a node
post.description: Records a build another tool runs on a machine, so others can see it (and cancel it). It is bookkeeping: nothing is started. The target machine must NOT be a configured transcode node: for a node, its own worker registers the lease (via="node_lease") and refusing is the worker's job; a node target without via answers 409 node_lease_required. 409 builds_paused means the operator paused builds on that node. Idempotent: send client_id ("bld_" and 8 to 59 letters, digits, _ or -) and repeat the same request after a network error; the same target and source returns the same build and creates nothing. Then heartbeat it while it runs and finish it at the end; a build without heartbeats is marked lost after its ttl. Answers 200 with the build (also when the same client_id is repeated); there is no 201. Errors: 400 invalid_request, 409 node_lease_required, builds_paused or build_id_taken.

source.description: The tool registering the build, e.g. a script name.

title.description: One line saying what is being built.

client_id.description: Optional idempotency key and build id: bld_ plus 8 to 59 letters, digits, _ or -.

holder.description: Optional who runs it (process or user label).

preempt_mode.description: Optional what transcoding does on this machine while the build runs (default suspend).

ttl_seconds.description: Optional lifetime without a heartbeat, in seconds. Omitted or 0 means 900 (15 minutes); a positive value is used as given (there is no minimum) up to 7200 (2 hours): a larger value is clamped to 7200, not refused. Negative is 400 invalid_request.

via.description: Only the worker of a node sends this.

200.description: The build (a repeat of the same client_id with the same target and source returns it as it is now, even ended, with the same 200).

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

get.description: One build record with its status, progress line, heartbeat and expiry times and exit code when it ended. 404 build_not_found for an unknown id (list builds with GET /nodes/v1/builds). Read-only.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

post.summary: Keep a running build alive (and report progress or log lines)
post.description: Called by the tool that runs the build, every few minutes, to say it is still alive and optionally to set a progress line, a new ttl and to append output lines (up to 256 lines of 300 characters per call, as often as every 2 seconds while the command prints; read them with GET /nodes/v1/builds/{id}/log). 409 build_ended (with the build in the answer) means the build is over, for example cancelled by an operator: stop the work. The body may be empty.

ttl_seconds.description: New lifetime without a heartbeat, in seconds. Omitted or 0 keeps the build's current window; a positive value is used as given up to 7200 (larger values are clamped to 7200, not refused). Negative is 400.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

409.description: code build_ended: the build already ended (finished, cancelled or lost, including a heartbeat after its expiry); body.build is its final record.

post.summary: End a build with its result
post.description: Called by the tool that ran the build when it is over. status is succeeded, failed or cancelled; exit_code optional. Finishing a build that already ended answers 200 with it unchanged. To stop someone else's build use POST /nodes/v1/builds/{id}/cancel instead.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

post.description: Marks the build cancelled. The tool that runs it learns on its next heartbeat (409 build_ended, status cancelled) and must stop. Cancelling does not kill any process by itself. Cancelling a build that already ended answers 200 with it unchanged. Operator action: use only when asked.

200.description: The build, now cancelled (or as it was if already over).

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

get.description: The last lines (up to 2000) the build sent with its heartbeats, each with an absolute number n. Pass after=N (the next_after of the previous answer) to get only newer lines; first_available is the number of the oldest line still held (older ones are gone). Numbers restart at 1 whenever the build's buffer is recreated (after a server restart, after the buffer was evicted or its retention passed and the build writes again), so every answer carries a generation naming the buffer the numbers belong to. Send it back as generation together with after: when it differs from the current one, or after is beyond the last line, the answer starts from the first line held and has reset true (discard what you kept and continue from next_after). Output is kept in memory for 30 minutes after the build ends and is lost on a restart (expired is true when it was dropped). Without wait the answer is immediate (poll again). With wait=S (1 to 25 seconds) and no line after N yet, the call is held until a new line arrives, the build ends, the buffer is dropped or recreated, or S seconds pass, and then answers exactly as it would without wait: an empty lines array on a timeout, so send the same after again. At most 64 readers wait at once (429 too_many_waiters, retry without wait). Read-only.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The generation of the previous answer. If it differs from the current one the answer is a reset from the start.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Long-poll: seconds to hold the call while there is no line after N and the build runs (0 to 25, default 0 answers at once).

generation.description: Names the buffer the line numbers belong to; empty when the build has no buffer. Pass it back as generation.

reset.description: true when your after/generation did not match this buffer: the lines start from the first one held and next_after is the new position.

401.description: Missing or wrong builds token (code unauthorized).

400.description: after is not a whole number of 0 or more, or wait is not a whole number from 0 to 25 (code invalid_request).

429.description: Too many readers are already waiting (code too_many_waiters); Retry-After: 1. Read without wait.

ApiKey.name: X-Api-Key
ApiKey.description: The builds token (web.builds_token_file). Authorization: Bearer <token> is also accepted.

code.description: Stable machine code: invalid_request, invalid_cursor, unauthorized, not_found, unknown_node, build_not_found, build_ended, build_id_taken, builds_paused, node_lease_required, internal.

hint.description: What to call instead or how to fix it.

status.description: waiting only appears on rows an earlier server left; it counts as active until Navigatorr cancels it.

expires_at.description: The build is marked lost if no heartbeat arrives by then.

status.description: running, or waiting on a record an earlier server left.

transcode.description: Transcode state of the node (read only here).
